what: Maplebear is Instacart. It delivers groceries from supermarkets that do not want to build their own delivery, runs the online storefronts for many of them, and sells advertising to the brands on those shelves.
customers: American households ordering groceries, the supermarkets whose stores it picks from, and the consumer brands buying ads.
money: fees from retailers and customers on each order
the smaller part but most of the profit
ads brands buy to appear in search results
moat: Relationships with most large American grocers at once, which gives shoppers the widest store selection and gives brands the largest grocery ad audience. Neither side is easy to rebuild.
risks: DoorDash and Uber have both pushed into grocery delivery with their own courier networks
Large grocers could build their own delivery and cut Instacart out
Revenue growth has slowed to roughly 10% a year
opportunities: $1.2B of free cash flow against a $13.7B market value, about 11 times cash flow
$687M of cash against $36M of debt, so the balance sheet carries no risk
The advertising business grows faster than delivery and costs almost nothing to serve
watch: Gross transaction value growth and advertising revenue as a share of the total.
